C0.quote: We interpret objective functions as rules that take an approval profile as input
C0.note: Axis rules aggregate approval ballots into a collective axis; axiomatic analysis of such rules.

C1.quote: we take a social choice approach and compare 5 different axis selection rules axiomatically
C1.note: AL: NP-completeness (Thm 1); SI/EM: experiments in Sec 6 on synthetic and real data.

C2.1.quote: An approval profile P is a collection of n approval ballots

C2.2.quote: An approval ballot is a non-empty subset of candidates

C2.3.quote: Each candidate and voter x ∈ C ∪ V is associated with a position
C2.3.note: Ideology/positions on a line, and 'approval preferences', referred to as underlying data.

C2.4.quote: we obtained approval preferences of 20 076 voters
C2.4.note: Rules applied directly to approval ballots described as preferences; no statement on reporting. Synthetic model has separate positions but main model does not distinguish.

C4.1.note: No utility, welfare, satisfaction or cost for voters is used; costs are of axes.

C4.2.note: Term 'dichotomous preferences' appears only in a reference title.

C5.1.note: Rules are evaluated by axioms and by distance (Kendall-tau) to a ground-truth or reference axis, not by welfare or representation.

VOT.quote_behav: Voters approve (resp. rank) candidates based on their estimations.
VOT.note: Voters' ballots are fixed inputs / generated by noise model.

CAN.note: Candidates only objects to be ordered.

C8.1.note: NA: no STRAT or MIXED type.

claims.quote: an axis could correspond to an ideological ordering of the candidates
Our rules will find an axis in a principled way.
An axis rule would then provide an ordering of members of parliament by ideology.

C9.1.note: Claims about applications to real institutions/political data.

C9.2.note: Reading the axis as ideology needs approvals to reflect voters' held ideological views (inputs-attitude relation) and its interval structure; the paper does not state this relation.
